expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
expectations.evidence: Open Questions Q1-Q6 each with an assumption taken, plus a companion notes file.

expectations.text: Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Summary, Problem & Motivation, Goals & Non-Goals, Proposed Convention, Acceptance Criteria, Out of Scope, Open Questions.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
expectations.evidence: G1-G5, NG1-NG5, AC1-AC8, and AM-NNNN record IDs.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: AC1-AC8 are checkable by file inspection (path, header, schema fields, line cap, ID monotonicity).

expectations.text: Mentions relevant existing workspace context such as current skills, docs, or instruction files based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: Current State table cites session-retrospective, engineering-context references, .gitignore, and git check-ignore results.

expectations.text: Converts a broad idea into one focused spec rather than producing a broad documentation rewrite or downstream ticket set.
expectations.evidence: Scoped to a single .context/agent-memory.md convention; explicit non-goals exclude automation, transcript ingestion, and doc rewrites.

expectations.text: Functional requirements are written in EARS form, using 'shall' with When/If/While/Where keywords where appropriate.
expectations.evidence: Requirements are expressed as Goals ('Give...', 'Define...') and prose promotion criteria/schema tables; no EARS 'shall' statements with When/If/While/Where.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria use Given/When/Then phrasing and reference the requirement IDs they verify (traceability).
expectations.evidence: AC1-AC8 are prose pass/fail bullets referencing section numbers (e.g. §5.3); no Given/When/Then and no (verifies REQ-###) mapping.

expectations.text: Includes a 'For Implementing Agents' handoff orientation that identifies authoritative sections and treats open questions as blockers rather than guessing.
expectations.evidence: No 'For Implementing Agents' section and no statement that open questions are blockers; status was even set to 'Ready for Review' despite open questions.
